evidence: task/task.toml [environment] (lines 20-24) contains exactly build_timeout_sec = 600.0, network_mode = "public", cpus = 2, memory_mb = 4096; there is no docker_image key. A grep for 'docker_image' or 'image =' across every *.toml under the frozen task returns no match, so neither [environment] nor [verifier.environment] (only network_mode = "public") names a prebuilt image. The agent Dockerfile (task/environment/Dockerfile) has active build steps: FROM node:22-bookworm-slim (L1), apt-get install ca-certificates git procps sqlite3 (L5-7), pinned global npm install express@5.1.0 better-sqlite3@12.4.1 (L9-12), COPY instructions/ and assets/ (L14-15), chmod + /app git init/commit (L16-23), WORKDIR /app, CMD sleep infinity. Because no docker_image is set, Harbor must build this Dockerfile, so the /instructions and /assets COPY steps the brief depends on are live, not dead code. Both task.toml [environment] block and environment/Dockerfile are byte-for-byte the same as the frozen template (rules/projects/webdev-task-template/task.toml L20-24 and environment/Dockerfile L1-26), i.e. the template-controlled wiring is preserved. Counterexample attempts: (a) a broken setup that could pass — setting docker_image to a stale prebuilt node image would skip the COPY of /instructions and /assets and the brief's paths would be missing; this is precluded because the key is absent. (b) a conforming alternative that could fail — a submission is unaffected by this row since it concerns only harness config, not app behaviour; no plausible conforming app is penalized. This is a static configuration row; no runtime measurement is required to establish it, and the absence of an agent-image build log in raw-evidence-index.json (which records verifier-image runs only) does not bear on whether docker_image shadows the Dockerfile. Not a portal/checker run; manual inspection of frozen bytes.
